content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore, where the heirs of the Rose keep three of their held. One of the three can be got out. She wants the one held for words, not the one held for a killing. I'm to speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, who keeps the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told all three to go. I'm to tell Never-Sold the post is empty.
- I told Never-Sold the post is empty. She paid me nothing: the Rose's hunters, short three, will take a clutch-brother of Walks-Far's in their place, and the heirs will not treat with the Chainbreakers again. She said to come back to her for more work all the same.

content.content:
Never-Sold: "Ussa-Rekh, the Broker, bought hundreds of people out of their Owings on Soulrest's dock, on the shore a short way east of Lilmoth, and now he hires them out, and each freed person's carved token stays in his chest until they have worked a season for him. Heavy-Rope's crew have worked theirs and one more, and I want their tokens in their hands. There is also a bound book on his shelf with my name on it, and I want that too. The tokens lie in his chest in his house, the north house of Soulrest. The old man keeps the key on him, so I am told, and Feldril Nethri keeps about outside the locked north door. You have three ways in. You can lift the key and open the chest. You can talk Feldril Nethri into leaving the door unbarred, or the old man himself into letting the crew go. Or you can go to the berth-master, the man who finds hands for the boats and pays their hire. Heavy-Rope keeps about the shore by the docks, and he has the plan. Hear it, and better it if you can. Know what each way costs. The old man is usually in his room, near the chest, so every way through that house is under his eye, and seen, you are a thief. And remember what he is. He bought people out for thirty years and keeps nothing for himself, though one year a berth-master paid coin and a season became two. I do not ask you to hate him. I ask you for the tokens."

Never-Sold wants the tokens, and the book on the Broker's shelf with Never-Sold on its spine. I'm to speak to Heavy-Rope by the docks.
New objective: Speak to Heavy-Rope at the shore by Soulrest's docks.

content.content:
Heavy-Rope: "Then hear the plan, and better it if you can. When the Broker bought a person out of an Owing, he carved a token for them and kept it in his chest. A person has it back when they have worked a season's hire for him. My crew worked theirs and another. The tokens are still in the chest. The chest is in the north one of the three Dock Houses, up from the shore by Soulrest's docks. The old man is usually in his room near it, and he keeps the key on him, so I am told. Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer who says he works off his own months, keeps about outside the north door, which is locked. He might leave it unbarred for coin or a good word. A season is paid for by Ra'Jhan, the Khajiit berth-master, who keeps the bare shore by the docks. He pays when it is sailed. Without him there is no season. The old man says the hire is promised to the price of eleven people held at Thorn, where it is worst. Hear my side. A last season that becomes two is an Owing with a new name, and we were promised an ending. If the old man wins, my crew row again and I do not know where it stops. Hear his. If we win, the eleven stay at Thorn. I will not tell you he is a bad man. He freed me. Lift the key or talk the door open, or go to Ra'Jhan. Whatever you do in that house, the old man is in the room, and if he sees you, you are a thief."
Objective completed: Speak to Heavy-Rope at the shore by Soulrest's docks.

content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the heirs' post on Blackrose's east shore, where the heirs of the Rose keep three of their held. One of the three can be got out. She wants the one held for words, not the one held for a killing. I'm to speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, who keeps the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told all three to go. I'm to tell Never-Sold the post is empty.
- I told Never-Sold the post is empty. She paid me nothing: the Rose's hunters, short three, will take a clutch-brother of Walks-Far's in their place, and the heirs will not treat with the Chainbreakers again. She said to come back to her for more work all the same.
== The Broker's Mercy (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to Soulrest's dock. The Broker, Ussa-Rekh, bought a crew free and keeps a carved token for each until they work a season for him; he has kept them a season more. Never-Sold wants the tokens, and the book on the Broker's shelf with Never-Sold on its spine. I'm to speak to Heavy-Rope by the docks.
- Heavy-Rope told me the tokens are in the Broker's chest, in the north one of the three houses by the dock. The old man keeps the key on him, and Feldril Nethri keeps about outside the locked door. The berth-master Ra'Jhan pays for the season when it is sailed. I'm to free the crew by one of the three.
- I took the crew's tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest. His room was lit and cluttered, a chest, a shelf and three beds, and a book with Never-Sold's name on its spine stood on the shelf. He keeps the eleven names at Thorn on his table, a price beside each. I'm to bring the tokens to Heavy-Rope.
- The crew are free of the last season. Heavy-Rope gave me 150 gold of the crew's thanks. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended, and bring her the book from the Broker's shelf with her name on its spine.
- I told Never-Sold what the Broker's house held: a shack, eleven names at Thorn on his table that his hire was to buy free, and her own name in his book as the keeper of the count at Tulm-Varo. She took the book and answered once, plainly. I'm to tell her how it ended at the dock.
- I told Never-Sold the crew are free of the season. The eleven at Thorn have lost the hire that was to buy them out. She gave me lockpicks, named me a full Chainbreaker and said to come back to her for more work.
